name: Mars
hook: The red planet, its war-god name and two tiny moons — Mars clues keep returning to the same orbit.

facts.label: the war god
facts.statement: Mars is named for the Roman god of war; his Greek counterpart is Ares, and the planet's two moons are named for the sons or attendants of Ares.

facts.label: Phobos & Deimos
facts.statement: Mars' two moons are Phobos (fear) and Deimos (dread); Phobos is larger and orbits so fast that it laps Deimos almost four times per Deimos orbit.

facts.label: Romulus & Remus
facts.statement: Romulus and Remus, the twins who founded Rome, were sons of Mars and the vestal virgin Rhea Silvia.

facts.label: Pathfinder
facts.statement: NASA's Pathfinder spacecraft landed on Mars on July 4, 1997, and deployed Sojourner, the first Mars rover.

facts.label: Mariner
facts.statement: Mariner 4 photographed Mars in 1965, becoming the first spacecraft to photograph another planet; Mariner 9 later took the first close-ups of Phobos and Deimos.

facts.label: The Planets
facts.statement: Gustav Holst's suite The Planets includes "Mars, the Bringer of War" as its opening movement.

facts.label: Gulliver's Travels
facts.statement: Jonathan Swift's Gulliver's Travels mentioned Mars' two moons 151 years before Asaph Hall discovered them.
